reason: The single cited study (E1) directly supports the formation of Hf-rich precipitates at interfaces, the hindrance of grain-boundary sliding and dislocation motion, and the improvement in high-temperature strength with unchanged room-temperature performance for the same alloy system and Hf content. However, the predicted quantitative strength improvement (>800 MPa) is not explicitly stated in the cited passage, and the claim about unchanged density is not addressed by the evidence.
premises: Hf addition (~0.5 at.%) induces fine Hf-rich precipitates at interphase boundaries
These precipitates hinder grain-boundary sliding and dislocation motion at high temperature
This improves high-temperature yield strength (e.g., from ~474 MPa to >800 MPa)
Alloy density is not significantly increased
